title: Pamtek says a ransomware attack on its business-system server may have exposed shareholder and former-employee data
date_note: Daily SECU gives 23 November as the attack date; the company notice was posted on 25 November.
geo_basis: Company is a KOSDAQ-listed Korean firm; the source gives no city, so the pin is at country level
summary: Daily SECU reports that KOSDAQ-listed Pamtek disclosed on 25 November that an external attacker carried out a ransomware attack on its business-system server on 23 November. Data possibly affected includes shareholders' names, addresses and share counts, and former employees' names, resident registration numbers and contact details. The company says no actual external leak has been confirmed so far, and it reported the incident to the Personal Information Protection Commission and KISA.
plain: Daily SECU reports Pamtek was hit by ransomware on 23 November. Shareholder and former-employee data may be exposed; the company says no actual leak has been confirmed so far.
exec: A listed Korean equipment maker says ransomware hit its business server; it has not confirmed that personal data actually left, per Daily SECU.
action: Pamtek set up a dedicated contact for damage reports and inquiries, its Management Planning Team (031-371-3112), per Daily SECU.
impact: Possible exposure of shareholder and former-employee personal data; the company says no external leak is confirmed.

validation.note: One publisher read (Daily Security), relaying the company's notice; the notice itself was not read.

review.note: Compared date, 25 Nov notice, data types, no confirmed leak, PIPC/KISA report and contact against Daily SECU; single_source correct
